title: What If Earth Froze Into a Giant Snowball?

scenes.text: What if Earth froze solid from pole to pole? Scientists think it happened, more than once.
Between 580 and 750 million years ago, glaciers reached the equator, at least on land.
Ice reflects sunlight, so more ice means more cooling, which makes even more ice.
The deep freeze may have lasted tens of millions of years. Some scientists say at least ten.
Volcanoes kept erupting beneath the ice, and their carbon dioxide slowly built up in the air.
Eventually that greenhouse effect melted everything. Some scientists still debate if the oceans froze fully.

description:
What if Earth froze into a giant snowball?
Glaciers likely reached the equator hundreds of millions of years ago, and volcanoes ended the freeze.
What should we run through next?
